key_insight: Recursive quantum optimisation can handle constrained problems by using broader problem classes that remain closed under variable elimination.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables recursive optimisation for problems such as knapsack and fixed-cardinality selection while keeping quantum evolution within feasible solutions.
method: Use correlations from variational quantum states to guide variable elimination.
Identify constraint classes closed under every elimination.
Efficiently construct feasible initial states and feasibility-preserving mixers for each reduced problem.
evidence_signal: Exact simulations on knapsack and vertex-weighted max-bisection instances show that the recursive scheme can outperform its non-recursive counterpart and penalty-based QAOA and RQAOA.
watch_item: Efficient constructions require restricted constraint structures; the abstract establishes simulation results, not practical quantum-hardware advantage.
